newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda denies Zaire claims of plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Uganda denies Zaire claims of plane crash.

text.p: Uganda on Wednesday denied a Zairean government claim that a cargo plane carrying Ugandan troops had crashed in eastern Zaire.
A senior Zairean defence ministry official said on Tuesday the plane crashed on Monday night on the Zairean side of the Ruwenzori mountain area.

"It was a cargo plane from Uganda. A contingent of Ugandan troops were on board," he said. "Several people died but the death toll is not known yet. The survivors have been captured by a group of Zairean soldiers who were around the crash site."
"There has not been any plane crash to the best of our knowledge in the last 72 hours," Ugandan Minister of State for Regional Cooperation Rebecca Kadaga told Reuters in Kampala.
"With modern technology I dont think even a helicopter can crash without being known. The area where they allege the plane crashed is a (rebel) Banyamulenge-held area," said Kadaga.
She questioned whether Zairean authorities would therefore have known about any crash when their army was not in the area.
Ruwenzori, 220 km (140 miles) north of the rebel headquarters in Goma, is close to Beni where the Zairean official said there was heavy fighting between the army and the rebels.

"There are no Ugandan soldiers in Zaire and the government of Uganda has no intention whatsoever to send troops," said Kadaga, calling on international monitors to fly to the region to prove the repeated accusations from Kinshasa were false.
